narrative:
The model predicts an 81% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this decision were your overall years of experience, whether you had received other job offers, and the sector you work in. Your relatively short total experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model expected to stay had longer careers, so your early-stage experience level strongly signaled higher turnover risk. 

Having received other job opportunities was the second most important driver and worked in the opposite direction, pulling the prediction slightly toward staying. The fact that you have been approached by other employers suggests you are valued in the market, which normally indicates loyalty. However, this positive effect was not enough to outweigh the other signals.

Your employment in the "other" sector, rather than medical or education, was the third key factor and increased the likelihood of leaving. This sector shows noticeably higher turnover patterns than the more stable fields where most stayers work.

The organization should discuss your career development goals with you openly. You may want to reflect on whether your current role matches your long-term plans, especially given the external opportunities you have received. Addressing experience-building and sector-specific challenges could help retain talent like you in the future. (248 words)
